hints.title: Chessboard Knight Move Probability Obstacle
hints.text: With each move, a knight chooses randomly among 8 L-shaped moves with equal probability 1/8. How can tracking the probability distribution across all chessboard squares over k moves calculate the total on-board probability?

hints.title: Equiprobable Move Transition Invariant
hints.text: The probability of being at square (r, c) after step s is 1/8 of the sum of probabilities of being at valid predecessor squares that can jump to (r, c) at step s - 1.

hints.title: Double-Buffered Step Probability Procedure
hints.text: Initialize an n x n board to 0.0 with 1.0 at (row, column). For each of the k moves, allocate a new board. For every square with positive probability, distribute 1/8 of that probability to each of the 8 knight moves that remain on the board. After k steps, return the sum of all values on the board.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: For each of K moves, scans N x N board updating at most 8 jumps.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recursive branching simulates 8^K paths which times out completely.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Maintaining two N x N probability matrices uses minimal O(N^2) memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using floating-point distribution across 8 moves per step.
